'''''Physostegia virginiana''''', the '''obedient plant''', '''obedience''' or '''false dragonhead''',<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | access-date = 14 January 2018}}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the mint [[Family (taxonomy)|family]], [[Lamiaceae]]. It is [[native plant|native]] to North America, where it is distributed from eastern Canada to northern Mexico.<ref name=grin/> ''Physostegia'' are known commonly as obedient plants because a flower pushed to one side will often stay in that position.<ref name=mo>[http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/gardens-gardening/your-garden/plant-finder/plant-details/kc/g620/physostegia-virginiana.aspx ''Physostegia virginiana''.] Missouri Botanical Garden.</ref> The name “false dragonhead” refers to the dragonheads of the related ''[[Dracocephalum]]'',<ref name=mo/> a genus to which the plant once belonged.<ref name=ns>[http://www.natureserve.org/explorer/servlet/NatureServe?searchName=Physostegia+virginiana ''Physostegia virginiana''.] NatureServe. 2012.</ref>

==Description==
It is a [[rhizome|rhizomatous]] [[herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] producing clumps of stiff, squared stems {{convert|2-4|ft|m|abbr=on}} tall. The leaves are lanceolate and toothed. The [[inflorescence]] is a long, dense raceme containing many tubular pink flowers which resemble [[snapdragons]]. The open fruit is shaped like a vase and contains four triangular, black seeds.

==Taxonomy==
There are two recognized [[subspecies]]. They are:
*''Physostegia virginiana'' ssp. ''praemorsa'' - Widespread further south, to [[Texas]] and [[New Mexico]].<ref name=usda>[http://plants.usda.gov/plant-profile?symbol=phvi8 ''Physostegia virginiana'']. USDA PLANTS.</ref> It has larger flowers, with sterile bracts below the inflorescence, and lacks rhizomes. It is typically found in dry upland sites such as prairies and glades.<ref name=Missouri>{{cite book |last=Yatskievych |first=George |date=2013 |title=Flora of Missouri, Volume 3 |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden Press |pages=356 }}</ref><ref name=Weakley>{{cite web |url= http://www.herbarium.unc.edu/flora.htm |title= Flora of the Southern and Mid-Atlantic States |author= Alan Weakley |date= 2015 |access-date= 2017-12-20 |archive-date= 2018-10-06 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20181006082209/http://herbarium.unc.edu/flora.htm |url-status= dead }}</ref>  
*''Physostegia virginiana'' ssp. ''virginiana'' - Found further north and west.<ref name=usda/> It has smaller flowers that lack sterile bracts. It is patch-forming from rhizomes. It is typically found in wetter habitats, such as streambanks and bottomlands.<ref name=Missouri/><ref name=Weakley/>

Cultivars of ''P. virginiana'' often do not fit well into either of the two varieties and are intermediate in character. They are thought to have originated from hybridization between the two subspecies.<ref name=Missouri/><ref name=Weakley/>
[[Image:Physostegia virginiana ssp virginiana.jpg|thumb|Subspecies ''virginiana'' has a smaller flower that lacks sterile bracts]]

==Cultivation==
[[File:Physostegia seeds.jpg|thumb|Seeds of ''Physostegia'']]
It is considered a good plant for adding late-season flowers to a garden. Fertile soils produce robust growth and wide spreading, and the plant may require staking. When it grows tall it has a "tendency toward floppiness" that can be controlled with [[pruning]]. It can be aggressive and dominate a landscape.<ref name=mo/>

===Cultivars===
Several [[cultivar]]s have been bred for color variety.<ref>[http://web1.msue.msu.edu/imp/modzz/00001089.html ''Physostegia virginiana''.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100729193925/http://web1.msue.msu.edu/imp/modzz/00001089.html |date=2010-07-29 }} Michigan State University Extension.</ref> Some ({{smallcaps|agm}}) have earned the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 78 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 25 April 2018}}</ref>

Cultivars include.
*'Alba' - white flowers.
*'Crown of Snow' - white flowers 
*'Pink Bouquet' - rose pink flowers 
*'Rosea' - pink flowers
*'Rosy Spire' - lavender-pink flowers
*'Summer Snow' ({{smallcaps|agm}})<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Physostegia virginiana'' 'Summer Snow'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/96263/Physostegia-virginiana-Summer-Snow/Details | access-date = 6 February 2021}}</ref> - pure white flowers
*'Variegata' - pink flowers, green and white variegated leaves
*'Vivid' ({{smallcaps|agm}})<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Physostegia virginiana'' 'Vivid'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/74299/Physostegia-virginiana-Vivid/Details | access-date = 6 February 2021}}</ref> - bright pink flowers
